disagreements.text: I tracked sleep against session quality for eleven weeks. Under seven hours the next day's intervals were 6-8 seconds per mile slower, every time bar one. Small sample, one runner, but it's consistent enough that I've stopped scheduling hard days after late shifts.

Everyone blames the hill at 18 miles. I split the field into people who ran the first half under 1:45 and over, and the slowdown after 18 was almost identical for both groups. If the hill were the problem the fast starters would fall apart harder.
